title: Memoize a Supplier: compute once, then serve the cache

blocks.text: Unless you memoize, every `get()` re-runs a Supplier's lambda. A memoizing wrapper turns "produce this value when asked" into "produce it once, then hand back the cached result".

Write `Memo.memoize(Supplier<T> source)`. The returned supplier calls `source` on its first `get()` and returns that same value on every later `get()` without calling `source` again. (As background, the page wraps the check-and-compute in `synchronized` so concurrent callers compute once too; the tests here call `get()` from a single thread.)

Each call to `memoize` makes a supplier with its own cache, even when the same `source` is wrapped twice. Think about a source whose honest answer is `null`, and about a source that throws the first time it is asked.

cases.says: The source runs on the first get(); later calls return the same cached value.
Wrapping the source runs nothing; the work waits for the first get().
A source that returns null is still asked only once, so null cannot mean not yet computed.
If the source throws, nothing is cached and the next get() tries again.
Wrapping the same source twice gives two memos, each of which asks the source on its own first get().

concepts: A memoizing Supplier computes once, caches the result and returns the cache on every later call.
A Supplier may return null, so a cache cannot use null to mean not yet computed.
